Mechanical Checks, Reproducibility & Provenance

Verification and trust boundary

All 6,463 declarations across the library and Solution.lean compile in Lean 4 and depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The five standalone Challenge endpoints (Theorem A(I–III), Theorem B, and Corollary C) and their proof dependencies also pass external kernel replay via NanoDa and con-ron, and Palomar's hosted mechanical preflight passed with zero errors on release v0.1.0.

Lean toolchain: leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc3 Mathlib commit: c55e6e786f49471c72fbddbec5415808896aec1e Permitted axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound

1. What is mechanically verified vs. what requires human reading

Following the Palomar verification architecture, statement review is separated from proof checking:

  • Whole-library compilation & axiom scan: All 6,463 declarations across the 388 library modules and Solution.lean compile in the Lean 4 kernel and pass Lean.collectAxioms with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound (zero sorryAx).
  • Standalone statement (Statement.lean → Challenge.lean) & external kernel replay: Statement.lean imports Mathlib alone and states the five headline endpoints (Theorem A(I–III), Theorem B, and Corollary C). Running lake comparator inside Bubblewrap compares the exported theorem statements and the declarations used in their types between Challenge.lean and Solution.lean (with proof bodies omitted) and replays those five endpoint proofs together with their transitive proof dependencies through the Lean 4 kernel, NanoDa, and con-ron.
  • Human review surface: No human expert has reviewed the Lean source files line-by-line. For the five compared Challenge endpoints, human mathematical review reduces to checking that the ~625 lines of Mathlib-only definitions in Statement.lean faithfully express the statements of the paper. For the remaining 41 body and appendix statements (some of which, such as Corollary 7.9 in ArtinTargets.lean, compile in the library outside Solution.lean's import closure), human judgment also applies to comparing their declarations in docs/PAPER-CORRESPONDENCE.md against the manuscript.

2. Summary of verification checks

Verification step Scope & recorded outcome
Source & module header check 392 Lean files inspected; all use the Lean 4 module system and stay well within the 10,000-line limit.
Library & Solution build lake build and lake build Challenge Solution pass cleanly (3,873 Lake build jobs).
Full declaration axiom scan Lean.collectAxioms across all 6,463 declarations in the library and Solution.lean reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound (zero sorryAx).
External kernel comparator Accepted by Lean 4 kernel, NanoDa, and con-ron on the five Challenge endpoints in comparator.json and their transitive proof dependencies.
Hosted Palomar preflight (Run 45530650450 ↗) Passed on proof tag v0.1.0 (f594ef1): zero errors; Solution build 317 s (2.13 GiB peak RSS), comparator 238 s (2.20 GiB), con-ron 100 s (1.84 GiB).

3. Reproducing the checks locally

python3 scripts/check-lean-sources.py
lake exe cache get
lake build
python3 scripts/audit_axioms.py
python3 scripts/scan_axioms.py
python3 scripts/generate_challenge.py --check
lake build Challenge Solution
./scripts/verify-comparator.sh

verify-comparator.sh runs on Linux with bwrap (Bubblewrap) on PATH and a real directory (not a symlink) at .lake/packages; see docs/VERIFICATION.md for details.
